title: Level 5 (World Class) - C-16
notes:
West leads the ♠10 against 6♥. If South makes the natural play of covering West's ♠10 with dummy's ♠Q, the contract will fail. East will cover with the ♠K and South will win the ♠A. South can draw trump and lead the ♠8 to knock out the ♠J and establish a winner with dummy's ♠9.

When East returns a club, South can do no better than to take the finesse (which is likely to lose due to West's unusual notrump overcall). If instead South wins the ♣A, and crosses to the dummy, dummy's spade winner will not help South. South will still have a diamond loser and, with West sitting over the ♣Q, no squeeze is possible.

Since an extra spade winner does not help South, he should duck West's spade opening lead in both hands to rectify the count for a minor suit squeeze against West. West, who cannot afford to attack clubs from his side of the table, switches to a trump. South should continue by unblocking the ♠A and crossing to the dummy in hearts in order to ruff a spade in the closed hand. South crosses again in hearts and dummy's last spade is ruffed.

South must continue by cashing the ♦A (a Vienna Coup) before running the rest of dummy's hearts (South had to be careful to unblock his hearts in order to win the next trick in the dummy). When dummy's last trump is played, West must keep his ♦K so will be forced to come down to a singleton club. South should read the position and drop the ♣K since West is very likely to have both minor suit Kings given his unusual notrump overcall.
